\section*{Question 5}

A population is modeled by a function \(P\) that satisfies the logistic differential equation
\[
\frac{d P}{d t}=\frac{P}{5}\left(1-\frac{P}{12}\right) .
\]
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] If \(P(0)=3\), what is \(\lim _{t \rightarrow \infty} P(t)\) ?
If \(P(0)=20\), what is \(\lim _{t \rightarrow \infty} P(t)\) ?
\item[(b)] If \(P(0)=3\), for what value of \(P\) is the population growing the fastest?
\item[(c)] A different population is modeled by a function \(Y\) that satisfies the separable differential equation
\[
\frac{d Y}{d t}=\frac{Y}{5}\left(1-\frac{t}{12}\right) .
\]
Find \(Y(t)\) if \(Y(0)=3\).
\item[(d)] For the function \(Y\) found in part (c), what is \(\lim _{t \rightarrow \infty} Y(t)\) ?
\item[(a)] For this logistic differential equation, the carrying capacity is 12.
If \(P(0)=3, \lim _{t \rightarrow \infty} P(t)=12\).
If \(P(0)=20, \quad \lim _{t \rightarrow \infty} P(t)=12\).
\item[(b)] The population is growing the fastest when \(P\) is half the carrying capacity. Therefore, \(P\) is growing the fastest when \(P=6\).
\item[(c)] \(\frac{1}{Y} d Y=\frac{1}{5}\left(1-\frac{t}{12}\right) d t=\left(\frac{1}{5}-\frac{t}{60}\right) d t\)
\end{itemize}
